overview: This Senate resolution mourns the death of Reverend Richard Smallwood, a gospel composer, pianist and arranger, and honors his life and work. It recounts his path from playing piano by ear at age 5 to studying at Howard University, forming the Richard Smallwood Singers, and writing songs such as "Total Praise" and "I Love the Lord" that were recorded by many well-known artists. It notes his eight Grammy nominations, his ordination as a minister in Washington, D.C., and his induction into the Gospel Music Hall of Fame. The resolution asks that copies be sent to his family, Howard University and the Metropolitan Baptist Church. The Senate approved it by unanimous consent on January 15, 2026.
for: Supporters say it is fitting for the Senate to recognize an artist whose music shaped modern gospel and is sung in churches across the country.
against: Critics say it is symbolic and doesn't change any law or spending.
